research_question: In hospitalised adult patients, what is the effect of medication review compared with standard care on all-cause mortality at the longest available follow-up?
outcome_description: All-cause mortality assessed at the longest available follow-up timepoint
positive_direction: Higher all-cause mortality in the medication review group compared with the standard care group
search_queries: medication review hospitalized patients mortality randomized controlled trial
inpatient medication review standard care mortality clinical trial
hospital pharmacist medication review all-cause mortality effect
inclusion_criteria: Hospitalised adult inpatients receiving a medication review intervention compared against standard care or usual care
Original empirical studies (e.g., randomised controlled trials, non-randomised controlled trials, controlled cohort studies) reporting all-cause mortality at any follow-up timepoint
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, commentaries, and conference abstracts without empirical data are excluded)
No comparison between a medication review intervention and a standard or usual care control group (e.g., studies comparing two active medication review interventions without a standard care arm)
No quantitative outcome data reported for all-cause mortality that allows calculation of an effect size (e.g., event counts, proportions, odds ratios, risk ratios, or hazard ratios)
Completely unrelated to medication review in hospitalised adult patients
moderators_to_extract: Study design (randomised controlled trial vs non-randomised controlled study)
Provider of medication review (e.g., pharmacist alone, physician, multidisciplinary team)
Hospital setting or ward type (e.g., general medical, geriatric, intensive care, surgical)
Length of maximum follow-up (e.g., in-hospital, 30 days, 90 days, 6 months, 12+ months)
Patient population age category (older adults / geriatric focus vs general adult population)
